chapter: Freelancing, Miller and the girls' bands
title: The Oak Grove Casino band at Bridgeport
summary: His band played a year at the Oak Grove Casino in Bridgeport with Freddy Webster, Buster Smith and others, earning a Walter Winchell write-up.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, then it said -- well, what about forming your own band in 1940? Do you remember that?
Yeah. That's the one I'm going to give you the picture of, on that location up there for 12 months.
The Oak Grove Casino in Bridgeport, Connecticut. At Myrtle Beach.
Who did you have in it, anybody --

Yeah. My brass section was Freddy Webster, and Joe Keyes and Eddie Rowan. And Eddie left there and went with Louis Jordan. And my reed section was Buster Smith and this here Billy White, and Lem Johnson was in that band, and John Stovall came up there when he left the Metropol.

But, let me see, now, who took Don's place? I brought another white boy in, Tony Pasco's brother, he was a (unintelligible). And that's when Walter Winchell give me a writeup, to be the best band of the year.

And I left there and went to Glenn Miller. After we stayed up there, it was held over 16 more weeks. That's all in that paper there. And that's when I let the band go, because Mrs. Kramer come up there and somebody from the union. And he was telling me, this band -- they're not going to let you through, you sound like a white band and you're hurting the bands over here.

And they was playing Harry James and all those bands. It's a pleasure beach two miles from here, and it's paying them a lot of money and you -- let alone standing room, you couldn't get on the highway. (Unintelligible) coming from Connecticut, because Bon Bon was singing in the band, too, and that's the type of band I had with --
Bon Bon was singing up there, too, with me.
